definitions.definition: u_t(x,t)=∂u(x,t)/∂t, the componentwise first time derivative.

definitions.type: family of componentwise spatial differential operators
definitions.definition: For each integer j with 1≤j≤n, ∂_{x_j} denotes componentwise differentiation in the jth spatial coordinate on R^n. Repeated subscripts denote iterated spatial derivatives, and ∂_{x_j}u_t differentiates u_t in that coordinate. Spatial gradients of u have rows ∂_{x_j}u; their Frobenius square is ∑_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u|².

inputs.statement: u:R^n×(0,∞)→R^m is jointly smooth (C^∞ in space and time).
For all x∈R^n and all t>0, |u(x,t)|=1.
For each x∈R^n and t>0 there exists a real scalar a such that u_tt(x,t)-Δ_xu(x,t)=a u(x,t). No regularity of a pointwise selection of these scalars is assumed.

output.statement: For every x∈R^n and t>0, u(x,t)·u_t(x,t)=0, u(x,t)·u_tt(x,t)=-|u_t(x,t)|², and for every j∈{1,…,n}, u(x,t)·∂_{x_jx_j}u(x,t)=-|∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|². Moreover u_t(x,t)·(u_tt(x,t)-Δ_xu(x,t))=0 and u_tt(x,t)-Δ_xu(x,t)=(∑_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|²-|u_t(x,t)|²)u(x,t). Any scalar a satisfying the pointwise normality equation is exactly ∑_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|²-|u_t(x,t)|².

binders.type: real scalar in the stated conditional equation

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary spatial point x.
At (x,t), choose a satisfying u_tt-Δ_xu=a u, as supplied by H005.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary x∈R^n and t>0. H001 makes the coordinate sums finite, and H002 permits componentwise product rules and equality of mixed derivatives. H004 gives u·u=1. Differentiating in time yields 2u·u_t=0, hence u·u_t=0. Differentiating once more yields 2|u_t|²+2u·u_tt=0, hence u·u_tt=-|u_t|². For each spatial coordinate j=1,…,n, two differentiations of the same unit constraint yield 2|∂_{x_j}u|²+2u·∂_{x_jx_j}u=0, hence u·∂_{x_jx_j}u=-|∂_{x_j}u|². These are routine product-rule calculations on the open domain R^n×(0,∞).

produces.statement: At the fixed (x,t), u·u_t=0, u·u_tt=-|u_t|², and u·∂_{x_jx_j}u=-|∂_{x_j}u|² for every j∈{1,…,n}.

argument.text: Choose the pointwise scalar a from H005. By F001, u_t·(u_tt-Δ_xu)=a(u_t·u)=0. Dotting u_tt-Δ_xu=a u with u and using H004 and F001 gives a=u·u_tt-∑_{j=1}^n u·∂_{x_jx_j}u=∑_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u|²-|u_t|². Substitution gives the stated explicit wave-map equation. The same calculation applies to any scalar satisfying the pointwise normality equation, so it also proves the assertion about every such scalar. No derivative or regular selection of a was used. Eliminate this pointwise witness and universally quantify the arbitrary x,t to obtain all asserted tangency identities and the explicit wave-map equation.
